design:
Decision 1: the contract is a file, not a parser. A check declares where its JUnit XML report lands. The Hub deletes that file before each run and reads it after the check ends. Console output stays for people to read, and no test id is taken from it.

Decision 2: re-running named tests is the operator's command, not the Hub's rewrite. A check declares a re-run command containing `{tests}`. The Hub substitutes the failing test ids and reads the re-run's own report. How a re-run is run, serially or in parallel, is the command's choice. A runner whose selector syntax differs from the id form gets a small wrapper script in the project. That keeps runner knowledge out of the product.

Decision 3: exit code decides pass or fail, and the report only names which tests failed. This keeps today's meaning of a failed check. A non-zero exit whose report names no failing test is a whole-check failure that names no test, so pytest's exit 3 needs no rule of its own.

Decision 4: no transition period with both paths. Keeping the pytest parser as a fallback would keep the debt this slice exists to remove. Existing checks without a report are judged as a whole until the operator adds one, and their result says so. This repository's checks get their report settings before the parser is removed, in the same build.

Decision 5 (operator, 2026-11-05): a test id is the testcase's classname and name, joined by '::'. These are the two attributes every runner writes. File plus name was rejected because it collides for same-named methods in different classes in one file and cannot select a class-based pytest test (hub/tests has 173 test classes in 39 files). A pytest-shaped id was rejected because it puts runner knowledge back into the Hub. The project's re-run wrapper translates ids into its runner's selectors.

lifecycle: The roadmap was approved on 2026-11-05. This slice is exploring until the operator approves it. It builds alongside slice 3 (quick checks at normal priority), and before slice 4, which shares project_checks.py and landing_queue.py with it. After the build, slice 2 (the known-failing list) is drafted with what this one taught.
problem:
The Hub decides which tests failed by reading pytest's console summary (`project_checks.py:808-873`). To re-run only those tests it rewrites the check's command, using a hard-coded list of about 30 pytest options, forcing `-n 0` and refusing any command containing shell characters (`project_checks.py:815-972`).

Any other test runner's failure can only be judged as a whole check. It is never confirmed per test, never compared with main per test, and never overridden. So a JavaScript or Go project gets a weaker gate than a Python one.

Pytest's own odd endings also fall through. On 2026-11-05, main's run in batch lbat-e7d9ae9007dc ended with exit 3 and a summary the parser could not use, so the batch was held for the operator.

JUnit XML is the structured result format that CI tools read. pytest (`--junitxml`), Jest and Vitest (junit reporters), Node's built-in runner (`--test-reporter=junit`), Go (gotestsum) and cargo-nextest all write it.

requirements.statement: Each check in a project's check settings can carry an optional report path, relative to the directory the check runs in, naming the JUnit XML file the check writes, and an optional re-run command containing the placeholder {tests}. Both are set through the app's check settings and the project settings route. A check saved before this change, or without them, reads as having neither. A re-run command without {tests} is refused on save with a message naming the placeholder.

requirements.rationale: The report is the runner's own statement of what failed; console output differs per runner and per version, and the pytest summary was cut off or missing in exactly the cases that held batches. Classname and name are the two attributes every JUnit writer fills (Decision 5).
requirements.statement: When a check that names a report ends with a non-zero exit and the report exists and is valid JUnit XML, the failing tests recorded for that check are exactly the testcases in the report that carry a failure or error element. Each has a test id of the testcase's classname attribute, followed by '::' and its name attribute. When the testcase has a file attribute, the file is recorded alongside the id for display and for telling whether the build changed it; it is not part of the id. No test id is taken from the check's console output.

A test that fails in a check's full run and again in a re-run of only that test is recorded under the same test id in both, so the Hub matches it across runs, across tasks and against main. Two different testcases in one report never share an id unless their classname and name are both equal.

requirements.rationale: A re-run in the same directory as the full run (project_checks.py:1055, :1061) would otherwise read the full run's report as its own.
requirements.statement: Before every run of a check that names a report, full or re-run, the Hub removes any file at the report path, so only a report the run itself wrote is read. A failing check that names no report, or whose report is missing, empty or not valid JUnit XML when the check ends, is judged as a whole by its exit code and names no failing test. Its result in the task's checks and the build's caught list says which of 'no report configured', 'report missing' or 'report unreadable' applied.

requirements.rationale: Keeps today's meaning of a pass; pytest's exit 3 (internal error) and similar endings need no rule of their own.
requirements.statement: A check passes or fails by its exit code and time limit exactly as before this change. A report naming failures on a check that exited 0 does not fail it. A non-zero exit whose valid report names no failing testcase is a whole-check failure that names no test.

requirements.rationale: Windows' command interpreter refuses a command line over 8,191 characters.
requirements.statement: Wherever the Hub re-runs a check's failing tests (confirming a failure is real, comparing with main, narrowing a landing batch), it runs that check's re-run command with {tests} replaced by the failing test ids, each passed as a separate argument, and reads the re-run's report by the same rules. A check with no re-run command, or whose re-run command with the ids substituted would be longer than 8,000 characters, is re-run as a whole with its own command.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-05: AgentWeave must be usable to build any type of project. Runner-specific parsing is what kept a non-Python check weaker and kept adding rules.
requirements.statement: The Hub's judgement of a check depends only on that check's settings, exit code, time limit and report. The Hub does not parse any test runner's console output for results and does not rewrite a check's command.

The check settings show the report path and re-run command for each check. They give a working example for pytest, Vitest or Jest, Node's built-in test runner, Go (gotestsum) and cargo-nextest. They say that test ids are the report's classname and name joined by '::', that a re-run command receives them as separate arguments, and that a check without a report is judged as a whole, with no per-test re-run or narrowing.

requirements.rationale: Re-runs are serial today by rule (a-red-main-does-not-hold-the-night FR-2): a timing test passed one parallel re-run and failed the next under load. After this slice that rule lives in the project's re-run command.
requirements.statement: This repository's hub-tests and sweep checks write a JUnit XML report and declare a re-run command that accepts classname::name ids, including tests inside classes, and runs them serially. The build delivers the exact check settings as text the operator can paste into the check settings, and the settings are in place before the pytest parsing is removed. With those settings, a failing Hub test, including one in a test class, is named, confirmed and narrowed per test, as it was before this change.

summary: A project check can name the JUnit XML test report it writes and a command that re-runs named tests. The Hub takes the failing tests from that report instead of parsing pytest's console output, and re-runs failing tests through the check's own command instead of rewriting a pytest command. A JavaScript, Go, Rust or Python project's check gets the same per-test judgement. A check with no report is judged as a whole by its exit code. The pytest-specific parsing and command rewriting leave the product. This is slice 1 of 'Checks any project can use, judged against a known-failing list'; slice 2's known-failing list needs these test ids.
